text: Risk management is the process of preparing for unexpected problems before they happen. It begins with identifying risks, which means carefully examining all parts of a project to see what could go wrong, such as delays, budget cuts, or technical failures. Once risks are known, teams develop mitigation strategies to reduce their impact, like breaking a large task into smaller steps or finding a backup supplier. However, not every problem can be avoided, so contingency plans are essential. These are clear action plans for worst-case scenarios, such as appointing a substitute leader if the main one becomes unavailable. Finally, risk management is not a one-time task. It requires constant monitoring to review the situation, update your assessment, and adjust your plans as new information appears. Good monitoring helps you stay in control rather than being caught off guard.
